name: Stash
description: Reference MVP manifest for upgrading Barony's existing Void Chest into a shared profile-persistent stash. This declares data and engine-owned hooks only; it does not request DLL/SO plugins, Lua/WASM, or arbitrary entity scripting.

inspirations.name: SMAPI manifest.json
inspirations.lesson: Use a stable unique id, user-facing name, version, and explicit required capabilities so loaders can identify compatibility before gameplay starts.

inspirations.name: Factorio info.json
inspirations.lesson: Keep the mod descriptor data-first and versioned; let the engine own load order, storage, and migrations instead of hiding behavior in an opaque fork.

inspirations.name: Fabric fabric.mod.json
inspirations.lesson: Separate required metadata from namespaced extension data and make dependency or compatibility failures clear to players.

barony.notes: Stash is intended as a small upstreamable native framework extension that coexists with Barony's official content systems. Existing content modding can package metadata/assets, while the framework supplies safe persistence and placement hooks.

capabilities.reason: The stash must survive death, victory, and starting a later run instead of living only in a normal save file.
The framework must expose a stable named inventory key that multiple Void Chest access paths can share.
Stash intentionally augments Barony's existing Void Chest behavior instead of creating a parallel chest mechanic.
Permanent Void Chest access points are needed in the lobby and in every generated shop.
The host must be authoritative for the shared inventory and clients need compatible framework metadata.

persistentStorage.description: Engine-managed per-profile storage for the shared Void Chest inventory. The engine may also mirror enough metadata into save data for resume compatibility.

void_chest_inventory.description: One shared stash inventory backed by Barony's existing Stat::void_chest_inventory and persisted across runs.

sourceBindings.description: Normal Void Chest open/close logic reads and writes this persistent inventory.
Void Chests created by spell effects use the same stash instead of a temporary per-run inventory.
Framework-placed lobby and shop access points open the same named inventory.

placements.description: Add one permanent Void Chest access point near the lobby assist shrine area.

targets.description: Resolve to a safe nearby tile after the lobby assist shrine is placed.

placements.description: Add one permanent Void Chest access point to every generated shop room.

targets.description: Resolve to a safe shoparea tile, ideally near the shopkeeper or counter if the engine can detect one.

multiplayer.notes: The host owns persistence and inventory mutation. Clients interact through normal Void Chest inventory networking and must use a compatible manifest/framework version.
